Subject: Internal: NovaHealth draft — proposed carve-out language and fallback options

Team —

I reviewed NovaHealth's note and their Order Form. High-level thoughts and proposed language below. Attaching a tracked-change redline of the Order Form (redline_orderform.docx).

1) Confidentiality & Trade-Secrets carve-outs from cap
Proposed: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, either party's liability for breaches of confidentiality obligations, or for misappropriation of trade secrets, shall not be subject to the aggregate liability cap set forth in the Order Form. For avoidance of doubt, this carve-out shall apply only to direct, provable damages resulting from such confidentiality breaches or trade-secret misappropriation, and shall not expand recovery for indirect or consequential damages which remain excluded."

Rationale: This preserves the customer's ask for meaningful relief while limiting runaway exposure by restricting recoverable items to direct damages and excluding punitive and consequential categories. It also keeps the carve-out narrowly tailored so we don't create a broad unlimited-exposure clause.

2) Alternative compromise (if procurement pushes harder):
Proposed compromise language: "In the event of a confidentiality breach or proven misappropriation of trade secrets, the aggregate liability cap shall be increased to an amount equal to the greater of (a) $5,000,000 and (b) two times the fees paid by Customer in the prior 12 months, solely for liability arising from such breach or misappropriation."

Rationale: Provides a quantifiable bucket rather than infinite liability — often acceptable to procurement and easier to underwrite with insurance.

3) Evidence & mitigation carve: require demonstration of provable loss, injunctive relief availability, and exhaustion of mitigation steps before certain remedies.

Attachments:
- redline_orderform.docx (tracked changes)
- proposed_cap_clause.txt (plain text of the two options above)

Next steps: Karthik — if you want to present option 1 (narrow carve-out) vs option 2 (quantified bucket) to Elena, I recommend we lead with option 1 and offer option 2 as a fall-back. If procurement insists on unlimited carve-out language, escalate to me and we can weigh insurance/exec approval.

Laura Bennett

Elena —

Thanks for your patience while we reviewed this internally. Attached is a proposed compromise we discussed with Legal. Two options (summary):

Option A (preferred): Narrow carve-out — confidentiality breaches and proven trade-secret misappropriation are carved out of the aggregate liability cap but limited to direct, provable damages; indirect/consequential damages remain excluded. (This preserves your ask while keeping recoverable categories constrained.)

Option B (fallback): Quantified bucket — in the event of a confidentiality breach or proven misappropriation of trade secrets, the liability cap for such event will be increased to the greater of $5,000,000 or two times the prior 12 months' fees, solely for liabilities arising from that event.

We recommend Option A as our starting point; Option B is available if procurement needs a fixed-number compromise for insurance/vendor review. If either option is acceptable, I can send a clean Order Form with tracked language (or a DocuSign link) for signature.
